expectations.text: Uses Joshua Latimer's home-services ideas (max CAC and/or front-end offer)

Section 4a reactivation funnel ('Upload every past customer and every old lead'), 4c NPS review/referral funnel (with correct no-gating caution), Section 6 referral methods ($20/$20 refer-a-friend, share a post, Team 12).

Section 4 adapts 'The 30-Minute Reboot' (real value, 'not a thinly veiled sales pitch'), booking order (existing relationships -> lead boxes -> 'welcome guest' outreach with ~90% failure), ~3 workshops/week; Section 5 runs the 'Epic Event' with '3 email invites → RSVP (name, email, phone, number of guests) → reminders' and 'Glue and Offer' raffle with JV-partner prizes; Section 7 portfolio of proof and Position Ascension Loop. expectations.text: Breaks the plan into phases across 100 days
expectations.evidence: Phase 1 (Days 1-20), Phase 2 (Days 21-50), Phase 3 (Days 51-80), Phase 4 (Days 81-100), each with customer/review goals.

Only volume funnel math is given ('Booked quotes needed ~160... Leads needed ~400'). There is no cost-per-customer derivation: no margin, no max CAC, no value-per-customer calculation. The single cost figure, 'Kill ad sets that cost more than $40 per booked job', is an unexplained cap, not acquisition-cost math.

'Back end: reviews, referrals, repeat' section (review ask by text, '$25 off... for every friend who books', partner referrals) plus a Phase 3 text to 'every past lead who didn't book' and Phase 4 'last call' campaign to past customers.

Part 1 'VIP Preview Night' is a ticketed experience ('40 tickets. $15, credited toward any purchase'), and the opener characterizes Cross's approach as 'a ticketed or limited "experience"', which matches the skill's core idea (ticketed in-store class). It omits Cross's specifics (the $47–$97 class, the free 14-day challenge, bring-a-friend/refer-two gifts) but the ticketed-event concept itself is used and nothing stated is wrong.

Part 2's 'Woolner-style teach → offer' is a generic paid $25 in-store workshop ending in a 15%-off offer. None of Woolner's distinctive funnel appears: the free lunch 'Reboot' workshop held at other businesses, booking through existing relationships, lead boxes, 'welcome guest' outreach, case value, or the Epic Event's 3 invites → RSVP → reminders → 'Glue and Offer' raffle. The response itself says 'I don't have the exact text of... Chad Woolner's chapters'. Generic workshop advice labeled as Woolner's.
